author: product-requirements-expert
title: A reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and its machine-readable form accept an optional specialty. When one is given, only veterinarians holding that whole specialty are listed, matched without regard to letter case; paging holds across the narrowed list. A blank or absent specialty lists everyone, as today.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time
given the same specialty, when the machine-readable form is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are returned
given a specialty name differing from the held one only by letter case, when either form is narrowed to it, then the same veterinarians are returned
given a name matching only the beginning of a held specialty, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is narrowed to it, then the request succeeds and no veterinarian is listed
given an empty or all-space specialty, when either form is narrowed to it, then every veterinarian is listed, as if none had been named
given a narrowed listing running to more than one page, when a later page is opened, then the narrowing still holds
non_goals: a visible specialty control on the directory page — the narrowing is asked for in the request only, this round
free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9, narrowed but standing)
narrowing by any veterinarian attribute other than specialty
notes: Owner-stated surface contract, carried here because the PRD names no addresses: an optional 'specialty' query parameter on /vets.html and on /vets. REQ-VET-003 (machine-readable form reinstated as a supported surface, fresh ID; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and unreused) is already met by shipped behavior — no work in this slice beyond the narrowing. Two open questions recorded in the PRD: whether a visible control follows, and whether a specialty with surrounding spaces is trimmed before matching (only empty or all-space is settled). docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-10-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md — outside my write scope, so it falls to the ADR owner.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: NG-9 is narrowed. Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing reuses the feature-package shape unchanged: a derived Spring Data query on VetRepository plus an optional request parameter on VetController's two existing routes, with no service layer and no new package (ADR 2026-07-31 feature-package-organization). Three things were not in durable memory and are now recorded. First, the owner's literal URL contract, written to docs/system-design.md as a new Contracts subsection 'Veterinarian directory URL contract' — the one section where the document is authoritative and the source follows. Second, the caching asymmetry: the two unnarrowed reads stay cached under 'vets', the specialty-narrowed reads are uncached (ADR 2026-08-10-vet-specialty-filter-uncached). Third, REQ-VET-003 reinstates the machine-readable route, so the stale Known Defects row calling it requirement-less was removed and the vet Contracts rows rewired to REQ-VET-003/004. Pagination links that carry a filter parameter are new to this codebase: the owner list's links carry only 'page'.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived queries traversing Vet.specialties to Specialty.name: a Page<Vet> overload taking Pageable for the HTML route and a Collection<Vet> overload for the JSON route. Name them so Spring Data derives an IgnoreCase equality match (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) — whole-name and case-insensitive fall out of the derivation, no JPQL string building.

VetController.showVetList gains an optional String specialty parameter; blank normalizes to absent and the controller falls through to the existing findAll(Pageable) path. Same normalization on showResourcesVetList, which keeps returning the Vets wrapper unchanged.

vetList.html needs the normalized specialty as a model attribute so every pagination link can carry it. Because an empty value is contractually equivalent to an absent one, the template needs no conditional link building.
CacheConfiguration and the 'vets' cache are untouched by this slice.

patterns.description: the optional-filter-plus-paging precedent: null or blank input widens to the unfiltered listing, a derived repository query takes the value and a Pageable, and addPaginationModel fills the same four model attributes. Mirror the shape, including String::strip; do NOT mirror the empty-result branch (rejectValue + return to the find form) — REQ-VET-004 requires HTTP 200 with an empty list, not a rejection.
derived query with paging (findByLastNameStartingWith) — the naming convention the new vet queries follow

risks.risk: The existing vetList.html builds hrefs with Thymeleaf preprocessing (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}). Interpolating the caller-supplied specialty that way inlines it into the URL unencoded, letting a crafted value inject further query parameters or a fragment into the link.
risks.mitigation: Build every pagination link with the parameterized link expression @{/vets.html(page=${...}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes each value. Convert the existing preprocessing links in the same edit. Never th:utext the specialty.

risks.risk: Annotating the new repository methods @Cacheable('vets') would key an unevicted, unbounded cache on an anonymous caller's string.
risks.mitigation: Leave the narrowed methods uncached — docs/adr/2026-08-10-vet-specialty-filter-uncached.md. The unnarrowed methods keep their annotations.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is ManyToMany(fetch=EAGER). A derived query produces an implicit join, so limit and offset still apply in SQL; rewriting it as a JPQL join fetch would make Hibernate page the collection in memory (HHH000104).
risks.mitigation: Keep the derived query. Cover the narrowing across a second page (theVetListShouldKeepTheNarrowingOnALaterPage) so a regression to in-memory paging is observable.

risks.risk: Whether a padded but non-blank value (' radiology ') is trimmed before matching is an open product question in the PRD; only empty and all-space are settled.
risks.mitigation: Strip once during normalization, mirroring owner search, and add no test asserting the padded non-blank case. Freezing an undecided behavior into the suite is the thing to avoid.

notes: Doc writes in this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (new Contracts subsection for the URL contract; vet Contracts rows rewired to REQ-VET-003/004; cache asymmetry sentence with ADR back-link; stale machine-readable-route defect row removed; Open Question 5 extended with the caller-controlled key space), docs/adr/2026-08-10-vet-specialty-filter-uncached.md (new), docs/adr/README.md (index rows for both 2026-08-10 ADRs, including the PRD author's non-goal ADR). No design-doc-autofix records were pending, so no autofix audit entries. Adjacent observation, out of this slice's scope and not written to docs: the owner list's pagination links carry only 'page', so paging an owner search silently widens it back to every owner. REQ-OWN-002 asserts nothing about paging a search, so it is not filed as a defect here.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Both specialty-narrowed repository methods (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, paged and unpaged) carry no @Cacheable annotation; the only two @Cacheable("vets") sites in src/main/java remain the pre-existing unnarrowed findAll overloads (VetRepository.java:45,55). The caller-chosen string never becomes a key in the unbounded, never-evicted vets cache. The Javadoc on both methods and docs/adr/2026-08-10-vet-specialty-filter-uncached.md record the reason, so a later contributor cannot re-add the annotation unknowingly.

All five pagination links in vetList.html now use the parameterized link expression @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}; no preprocessed @{'...?page=__${i}__'} form remains in that template. Thymeleaf URL-encodes each parameter value and HTML-escapes the attribute, so a crafted specialty cannot inject a further query parameter or a fragment into a link. VetControllerTests.theVetListShouldKeepTheNarrowingOnALaterPage asserts the rendered link carries the encoded & separator, which regresses if the form reverts.

Injection: the narrowing reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), which bind the name as a JDBC parameter. No JPQL or SQL string is built from the parameter, matching the threat-model row on SQL injection in docs/system-design.md.

XSS: the specialty is never rendered as text, only as an encoded URL parameter; a repository-wide sweep found no th:utext anywhere in src/main/resources/templates. The /vets JSON route serializes through Jackson under application/json.

Input normalization: VetController.narrowing maps null, empty, and all-space alike to the empty string, and an empty narrowing falls through to the unnarrowed path — no null reaches the repository and no partial-value branch exists to confuse.

No new attack surface elsewhere: the change set touches no build, dependency, or configuration file (no gradle/pom/properties/yml in the changed-file list), so the dependency graph is identical to the reviewed baseline and no supply-chain delta exists for this pass. A scan of the added lines found no hardcoded credential, token, or key.

Residual pre-existing items, out of this slice's scope and correctly left alone: the vets cache remains unbounded on its already caller-controlled Pageable key (system-design Open Question 5), and the preprocessed pagination links in owners/ownersList.html interpolate only server-derived integers.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The same concept carries three different names within one small class: the request parameter is `specialty`, the normalized value is a local variable and a private method both named `narrowing` (a gerund, not a noun a reader can hold onto), and it is written back into the model under the key `specialty`. The mirrored precedent this slice was told to follow (OwnerController.processFindForm) keeps its normalized value named `lastName` end to end, param to model attribute. A reader has to track that `narrowing` and `specialty` are the same string here, with no such mapping to track in the file it mirrors.
findings.fix: Rename the local variable and every call-site occurrence from `narrowing` to `specialty`; rename the private helper method to a verb name such as `normalizeSpecialty(String specialty)` so the concept has one name from the `@RequestParam` to the model attribute.

approved_aspects: VetRepository's two new derived-query methods are well-named (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), Javadoc-documented including the deliberate no-caching rationale with a back-link to the ADR, and match the existing `<code>` Javadoc style already used in this file

The pagination links in vetList.html were correctly converted from Thymeleaf's unsafe string-preprocessing form to the parameterized link-expression form for every link, closing the injection risk the design review flagged, with no link left in the old form
The controller correctly reuses the existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel shape and needs no new branch for the empty-result case, matching the PRD's HTTP-200-with-empty-list requirement
./gradlew checkFormat passes with no violations

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The design-block risk register (line 8) named this exact test as the mitigation for a Hibernate paging regression: 'Vet.specialties is ManyToMany(EAGER), a derived query keeps limit/offset in SQL; rewriting it as a JPQL join fetch would make Hibernate page the collection in memory (HHH000104). Cover the narrowing across a second page (theVetListShouldKeepTheNarrowingOnALaterPage) so a regression to in-memory paging is observable.' The test carrying this name is a @WebMvcTest with vetRepository fully Mockito-stubbed (given(...findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(eq("radiology"), any(Pageable.class))).willReturn(new PageImpl<>(...))). A stub returns whatever PageImpl it is told regardless of how the underlying query is actually written, so this test cannot observe a regression to in-memory paging at all — it only proves the controller forwards the page number and renders the model. No test anywhere in the diff pages a narrowed query against the real repository/H2. data.sql seeds exactly 2 vets holding 'radiology' (vet_specialties rows (2,1) and (5,1)), so a real second-page assertion is directly available: page the narrowed query with a Pageable of size 1 and assert page 2 (index 1) still returns only a radiology-holder, mirroring ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialty but with a real Pageable instead of Pageable.unpaged(). Until that exists, the risk the design triage flagged as needing a regression guard has none.

testing-principles.md § Test Naming requires the BDD school 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}' for tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. All five new ClinicServiceTests methods use the pre-school 'should...' form instead (e.g. shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialty, not the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). This is a real inconsistency within the same changeset: the sibling new tests added in VetControllerTests in this same diff (theVetListShouldShowOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetJsonShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, etc.) correctly follow the school. Swept the class for other new-test instances of the pattern — these five are the complete set.
findings.fix: Rename the five methods to the {Subject}Should{Outcome} form, e.g. theVetSearchShouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialty, theVetSearchShouldMatchRegardlessOfLetterCase, theVetSearchShouldNotMatchAPrefixOfASpecialtyName, theVetSearchShouldFindNoVetsForASpecialtyNoneHolds, theVetSearchShouldFindEveryVetHoldingASpecialtyUnpaged.

findings.description: The design-block risk register flags un-encoded interpolation of the caller-supplied specialty into pagination hrefs as an injection vector, mitigated by switching to the parameterized Thymeleaf link expression @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. theVetListShouldKeepTheNarrowingOnALaterPage asserts the rendered href only for the benign value 'radiology'; no test exercises a specialty value containing a URL-structural character (e.g. '&', '#', or a quote) to confirm the link expression actually encodes it rather than letting it inject an extra query parameter or break out of the href attribute. This is exactly the boundary-testing category (special characters in input) the checklist calls for, and it is the one risk the design triage flagged as needing a mitigation test.
findings.fix: Add a VetControllerTests case stubbing a specialty value containing '&' (e.g. "cardio&page=99") and asserting the rendered pagination href HTML-encodes it (content().string(containsString("specialty=cardio%26page%3D99")) or equivalent) rather than injecting a raw '&page=99'.

approved_aspects: The two deliberate carry-overs both hold up under review. (1) Query semantics — whole-name match, case-insensitivity, prefix non-match — are genuinely covered, just under different test names and in a different file (ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyRegardlessOfLetterCase, shouldNotFindVetsByAPrefixOfASpecialtyName) than the PRD's suggested VetControllerTests names. Confirmed by running the tests with --info: the case-insensitive test executes real Hibernate SQL (`where upper(s1_1.name)=upper(?)`) against H2, so it exercises the actual derived-query semantics. Asserting the same criteria at the @WebMvcTest layer, where vetRepository is a Mockito stub, would only prove the controller forwards its parameter unchanged to a stub matched by exact-string equality — it would assert the mock, not the matching behavior, exactly as the implementer judged. No gap here. (2) The padded-but-non-blank input (' radiology ') is correctly left unpinned: docs/prd.md Open Questions records trimming as an open product question, and design-block line 8 explicitly directed no test freeze it. Confirmed absent from both test files.

VetControllerTests.theVetListShouldListEveryVetWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank and theVetJsonShouldReturnEveryVetWhenTheSpecialtyIsBlank correctly exercise the all-space boundary case, matching the settled part of the PRD's open question.

notes: Fix dispatch for the doc-reviewer clarify finding at line 18; deliberately NO supersedes_record_at — this is a prose fix, not a re-triage, so the round's other approvals stand. Finding accepted as stated. The old heading, 'Veterinarian Search Narrowed to Free-Text Search Only', parses with 'veterinarian search' as its subject, so at a glance it grants a search capability limited to free text — the inverse of the decision. The intended subject was NG-9, which is invisible in the heading. New heading: 'Free-Text Veterinarian Search Stays Out of Scope; Narrowing by Specialty Is In'. It names the non-goal outcome first, matching the sibling convention in 2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md, and I added the second clause beyond the reviewer's suggested wording because this ADR is the record prd.md NG-9 and the system-design.md URL-contract subsection both cite as the decision that ADMITTED the narrowing; a title naming only the non-goal would read in the index as though nothing was granted. 'Veterinarian' over 'Vet' per ubiquitous-language (Vet is the code and page-text short form; Veterinarian is the prose term). Two files changed, heading lines only: the ADR line 1 and its docs/adr/README.md index row. The filename keeps the load-bearing non-goal- infix. Cross-reference sweep of docs/ and src/ found no other occurrence of the old title string — prd.md (Non-Goals preamble and the NG-9 row) and system-design.md both link the ADR by path with generic link text, so neither needed an edit. ADR body left untouched: 'Narrow NG-9 to free-text search' in Options Considered takes NG-9 as its explicit subject and does not carry the ambiguity. Autofix audit: the log contains no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to judge.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix delta introduces no new attack surface. The VetController change is a rename (narrowing -> normalizeSpecialty) plus in-place reassignment of the @RequestParam parameter in both handlers; the normalization body is byte-identical (null -> "", otherwise strip()), the empty-narrowing fallthrough to the unnarrowed repository call is unchanged, and no null or partially-normalized value can reach the repository. Reassigning a handler parameter happens after Spring MVC binding and cannot affect binding, conversion, or the model attribute, which is fed the same normalized value.

The new boundary test VetControllerTests.theVetListShouldEncodeASpecialtyCarryingUrlStructureIntoItsPaginationLinks does pin the encoding behavior for the injection vector assessed in round 1. It drives the real Thymeleaf render with specialty="cardio&page=99" and asserts the href contains specialty=cardio%26page%3D99 -- both the & and the = percent-encoded, so the value cannot break out into a further query parameter. The negative assertion (no specialty=cardio&page=99) closes the specific regression shape, a preprocessed @{'...?page=__${i}__&specialty=' + ${specialty}} concatenation, which would emit exactly that string. A regression emitting a raw unescaped & would still fail the positive assertion, so the pair covers both reversion shapes rather than only the literal one.

Constraint 1 re-verified in the working tree: the two @Cacheable("vets") sites in VetRepository.java remain on the unnarrowed findAll overloads (lines 45 and 55); neither findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase overload (lines 72 and 87) carries the annotation. The caller-chosen string still never becomes a key in the unbounded, never-evicted vets cache.

Constraint 2 re-verified: all five pagination links in vets/vetList.html (lines 30, 35, 40, 45, 50) remain on the parameterized link-expression form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. No preprocessed string-concatenation form was reintroduced. A repository-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates found no th:utext and no unescaped inlining, so the specialty is still never rendered as text.

ClinicServiceTests delta is a @DataJpaTest paging assertion against H2 plus five renames; no security-relevant surface. The two docs files changed only a heading line. No build.gradle or dependency-manifest change in the delta, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged since the round-1 pass and no new CVE exposure is introduced.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Real progress on the round-1 blocked finding: the stub-based VetControllerTests test is now backed by a genuine @DataJpaTest against H2 with no stub, and it correctly proves paged narrowing executes real SQL rather than a mocked PageImpl. But the implementer's own disclosure is accurate and matters: radiology's two holders (vet_specialties rows (2,1) and (5,1) in src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql) each hold exactly one specialty, so a regression to a JPQL join fetch over the EAGER specialties collection would produce exactly one joined row per matched vet here too -- no row inflation, so SQL-level LIMIT/OFFSET would coincidentally still return the same totalElements/totalPages/content this test asserts. HHH000104 would print to the log under the regression, but nothing in the test fails on it. The design-triage risk register wanted a guard that observably fails on this regression, and this test would pass silently under the exact defect it's named for -- the risk still has no deterministic guard. This is fixable without touching the shared production seed file (which would be a product-visible change to demo data, reasonably avoided): @DataJpaTest runs each test in its own rolled-back transaction, so the test itself can attach a second specialty to one of the radiology holders (e.g. autowire a Vet/Specialty via the repository, add 'surgery' to vet id 5, save, flush) before paging, making a real vet->specialty row inflation exist only for the duration of this test. With that, a join-fetch regression would return duplicate rows for that vet, and in-memory pagination would produce a different second page than SQL-level pagination does, which the existing assertions would then genuinely catch.
findings.fix: In theVetSearchShouldNarrowOnALaterPage, before paging, use the injected VetRepository (or an autowired specialty repository) to add a second specialty to one of the two radiology holders and save/flush it inside the test's own transaction, so the query has a vet with 2 matching-branch specialties and a join-fetch regression produces an observably different paged result. Do not modify src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql -- it is shared production seed data.

approved_aspects: The naming autofix from round 1 is fully applied: all five ClinicServiceTests methods now use the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school, consistent with the sibling VetControllerTests names in the same diff.

The encoding autofix from round 1 is correctly implemented: theVetListShouldEncodeASpecialtyCarryingUrlStructureIntoItsPaginationLinks stubs a specialty value carrying URL-structural characters ('cardio&page=99') and asserts both that the encoded form appears in the rendered href and that the raw unencoded form does not -- this is the exact boundary-testing gap the round-1 finding named, now closed.

Ran the two touched test classes (ClinicServiceTests, VetControllerTests) with --info: both pass, and the Hibernate SQL log for the narrowed query confirms LIMIT/OFFSET stay in the generated SQL for the current implementation.
The padded-but-non-blank input remains correctly unpinned, matching the still-open product question in docs/prd.md.
